title: Dark state as a measurable state by a dispersive readout without a Purcell limit
authors: Wei-Chen Chien, Jyh-Yang Wang, Yen-Yu Chiang, Cheng-Chengh Huang, Lih-Chieh Hsaio, Yen-Chun Chen, Cen-Shawn Wu, Chiidong Chen, Watson Kuo
abstract: It is believed that the enhancement in qubit-resonator coupling allows a better dispersive readout but introduces greater Purcell loss. In this work, we propose that a dark mode in a coupled quantum system may violate this rule by introducing the ZZ interaction between the dark and a bright mode. The dark mode may exhibit an effective zero coupling strength, and zero Purcell loss with the resonator photons. Nevertheless, the dispersive shift is almost the same as the bright state, due to the higher order perturbation introduced by the higher excited states. Such a state demonstrates the measurability without a Purcell limit in circuit quantum electrodynamics.
summary: This paper proposes and experimentally demonstrates a 'dark mode' in a coupled superconducting qubit system that circumvents the Purcell decay limit inherent in high-coupling regimes. By utilizing a specific ZZ-type interaction, the dark state achieves near-zero radiative loss while remaining distinctly measurable via dispersive readout techniques. This breakthrough paves the way for building more robust and scalable quantum hardware.
main_problem: The paper addresses the trade-off in circuit quantum electrodynamics (cQED) between achieving strong readout coupling and minimizing Purcell decay, which limits qubit lifetime.
main_result: The authors demonstrate a measurable 'dark mode' in a coupled quantum system that exhibits zero Purcell loss while maintaining a dispersive shift comparable to the bright state.
method: The study combines theoretical analysis (perturbation theory) with experimental measurements, including two-tone spectroscopy, time-resolved Rabi oscillations, and single-shot readout.
model_or_system: The system uses two capacitively coupled X-mon qubits coupled to a readout resonator, forming a minimal 3-body model. The physics is analyzed by identifying and characterizing the resulting bright and dark collective modes.
key_observables: Dark-state-dependent dispersive shift, suppressed resonator coupling, distinct long coherence times ($T_1$), and measurable AC-Stark shifts.
important_parameters: The experiment operates in the dispersive readout regime (1-2 GHz detuning) with specific coupling strengths ($g/\hbar \approx 53 	ext{ MHz}$; $g_{Q}/\hbar \approx 211 	ext{ MHz}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Rotating-Wave Approximation (RWA), and the Purcell limit study uses a phenomenological relaxation rate.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the proposed 3-body model, energy repulsion in the RWA manifold, the photon-number-dependent AC Stark shift of the dark mode, and experimental readouts (IQ plots, Rabi oscillations) confirming state distinguishability.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the theoretical model and the problem of Purcell loss. It then details the experimental setup using coupled transmons and proceeds through state characterization, loss measurement, and finally demonstrates the measurable nature of the dark state via dispersive readout.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, experimentally realized mechanism to engineer quantum states that are robust against environmental decoherence (Purcell loss) while remaining accessible for quantum measurement, which is a major goal in building scalable quantum processors.
